status: Default ScreenBuffer compares each preparation with submitted content; reverted pending changes no longer transfer
production_consumers: Nine shared screen-space vertex streams across main/dialog profiles
retired_paths: Updating the comparison snapshot before submission
Union/sort of all superseded dirty ranges
Discarding valid submitted snapshot contents on cancellation
behavior: Keep submitted and prepared content separate. Every changed preparation replaces the pending plan with exact aligned differences against submitted content. Returning to the submitted bytes cancels the plan entirely.

Commit the prepared snapshot at the existing successful frame-upload boundary; both production callers immediately submit the resulting batch. Allocation replacement invalidates the old baseline; failed allocation admission preserves it. Cancellation preserves valid submitted bytes for an exact retry.

Swap and reuse two bounded CPU snapshot allocations across changed frames, avoiding new allocation or a second full copy per frame. Each retained snapshot is at most 256 KiB: up to 512 KiB payload per stream, or 4.5 MiB for nine fixed streams, plus separately outstanding metadata/headers. Terminal quad snapshots similarly use up to two 96-byte payloads.

Oversized prepared content is released after submission/cancellation and still bypasses snapshot retention. Empty streams release all owned snapshot/range storage. GPU capacities, staging admission and shader/painter behavior remain unchanged.

proof.renderer: 327 renderer tests pass; 11 diagnostic/visual cases filtered. New actual-GPU test verifies 1,000 changed/reverted preparations produce zero transfer descriptors, cancellation preserves submitted bytes, retry uploads only changed words, and 100 changed submissions reuse the same two allocations with final readback parity. Existing cold/replacement, cap/bypass, shrink/regrow, budget refusal, shared control/text and upload regressions pass.
proof.development: Initial focused run found two stale expectations: a shrink/regrow before submission retransferred unchanged tail bytes, and cancellation forced a full retry. Updated them to require only real dirty bytes while retaining GPU readback. Other existing diff assertions now establish their GPU baseline through a real flush. Failed focused receipt preserved.
proof.lint_build: Visual renderer/app all-targets Clippy -D warnings and fresh application build pass. Source health 2,263, dependency and governance gates pass.
proof.drift: Full drift stops at the existing console-routine-focused 1x mismatch: 3,778 pixels (0.384318%), dat-console-revision-golden-hrak. Earlier gates pass; later gates unrun; no full-drift acceptance.

limits: This increases maximum retained screen snapshot payload from one to two 256 KiB allocations per stream; it is a bounded implementation tradeoff, not an unchanged-memory or RSS acceptance claim. Full CPU metadata/peak/aggregate admission and qualification remain open.

Over-cap content still bypasses comparison retention. Complete actual transfer-boundary counters must distinguish dirty destination payload, protocol metadata and GPU packet copies. No REUSE-SCREEN, MEM-01, S4/S5 or issue closure.

Other S4 resource/shaping work and S5 native/backend/fault/fairness/endurance/independent qualification remain. Preserve GEFN, separate concurrent multi-device failure and nonblocking resize exclusion. No dependency, vendoring, license, prototype or specification amendment.
